cards.title: Human CL Prediction Method Performance
cards.claim: In the 19-drug subset analyzed, in vivo methods (particularly two-species allometry, rat-dog) generally performed better than IVIVE methods for predicting human intravenous clearance. Maximum success rates for predicting human CL were 100% (10-fold error), 94% (threefold), and 78% (twofold).
conditions: Applicable to prospective human PK simulation
Requires preclinical in vivo data from at least two species (typically rat and dog)
IVIVE methods require specific binding assumptions (microsomal/plasma binding)
required_inputs: Preclinical in vivo clearance data (rat, dog)
In vitro microsomal/hepatocyte stability data (for IVIVE)
Plasma protein binding data (for IVIVE binding corrections)
limitations: Abstract-only source; full methodology details unavailable
Performance metrics are aggregate across 19 drugs; applicability to specific target drug unknown
IVIVE accuracy varies significantly with binding assumptions
cards.downstream_use: Selecting appropriate translation method for human PK simulation; justifying use of allometry vs. IVIVE based on available data types

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
